subject.title: fix: allow trusted host-read html after outbound staging

question: Should OpenClaw accept SHA-256 plus byte-size provenance in the shared state database as the permanent trust mechanism for generated HTML copied into media/outbound and later reloaded with host-read enabled?
rationale: The implementation is correct, narrowly scoped, and fail-closed, but changing what evidence authorizes local HTML outside the original trusted root is a security-policy choice requiring maintainer intent.

options.title: Accept content-bound provenance
options.body: Approve the exact-byte staged trust lifecycle and merge after the current-head mergeability and required checks settle.

options.title: Keep temp-root-only trust
options.body: Reject this boundary extension and redesign delivery so trusted HTML is never reauthorized from outbound staging.

recommendation.title: Accept content-bound provenance
recommendation.body: Approve the exact-byte staged trust lifecycle and merge after the current-head mergeability and required checks settle.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored and merged the existing trusted generated HTML boundary and are the strongest available owner for extending it.
